The Maisa mobile app brings public social care and health care services directly to your phone. You can now manage your and your family's health care and social care anywhere, anytime. Exchange messages with your care team, access your medical and social care records, view your test results and manage your appointments.

The Maisa portal allows you to
• ask for advice or ask to be contacted
• review and supplement your social care and health care information
• view tests results
• book and cancel appointments
• fill in questionnaires prior to your appointment
• upload self-monitoring results from apps such as Apple Health
• connect with a provider through a video appointment
•	arrive yourself for a scheduled appointment using the Appointment Arrival feature. Please note that this feature requires access to your device’s location in the background.

The Maisa application is available in Finnish, Swedish and English. Maisa is used in the services of HUS Helsinki University Hospital, the city of Helsinki and in the services of Vantaa and Kerava wellbeing services counties as well as Kauniainen (as part of the Western Uusimaa wellbeing services county).

So what is HRV?
HRV is a measure of your autonomic nervous system that is widely considered one of the best objective metrics for physical fitness and determining your body’s readiness to perform.

Although HRV manifests as a function of your heart rate, it actually originates from your nervous system. Your autonomic nervous system, which controls the involuntary aspects of your physiology, has two branches, parasympathetic (deactivating) and sympathetic (activating).

The parasympathetic branch (often referred to as “rest and digest”) handles inputs from internal organs, like digestion or your fingernails and hair growing. It causes a decrease in heart rate. The sympathetic branch (often called “fight or flight”) reflects responses to things like stress and exercise, and increases your heart rate.

Heart rate variability comes from these two competing branches simultaneously sending signals to your heart. If your nervous system is balanced, your heart is constantly being told to beat slower by your parasympathetic system, and beat faster by your sympathetic system. This causes a fluctuation in your heart rate: HRV.
